newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Taeil in money squeeze, denies defaults.
newsitem.headline: Taeil in money squeeze, denies defaults.

text.p: South Korea's Taeil Media Co Ltd said on Friday it had been facing temporary liquidity problems but it strongly denied market rumours the computer part producer was on the brink of defaulting on its debts.
"We are temporarily facing cash flow problems as other Korean companies have experienced," said spokesman Kang Sung-il. "But it's not true we will default on our debt obligations."
Kang said a Taeil affiliate was negotiating with its creditors to extend loan payments due on Saturday. Taeil extended payment guarantees for the unit to creditors.
"The talks with creditors have been distorted in the market to make it sound like we are facing default on debts," he said.
"We are afraid the rumours will deal a serious blow to us as financial institutions are now reacting nervously whenever there are such vicious rumours, he said.
Kang said Taeil would post 16 billion won in net profit in calendar 1997 with the introduction of new products, against eight billion won last year.
"If we can pass the critical point successfully, we can meet the profit target," he said.
